hypothesis: If the claim holds, Perissodactyla and Leporidae form a clade in the current synthetic mammal phylogeny that excludes the other ungulates (Artiodactyla; also Proboscidea and Hyracoidea in the 1917 sense of Ungulata) and excludes the rodents.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Take the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree (induced_subtree API, current synth version) over these tips: Perissodactyla = Equus caballus, Ceratotherium simum, Tapirus terrestris; other ungulates = Bos taurus, Sus scrofa, Camelus dromedarius (Artiodactyla), Loxodonta africana (Proboscidea), Procavia capensis (Hyracoidea); Leporidae = Oryctolagus cuniculus, Lepus europaeus, Sylvilagus floridanus; other lagomorph = Ochotona princeps; Rodentia = Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus, Sciurus carolinensis, Cavia porcellus, Castor canadensis; outgroups = Canis lupus, Homo sapiens, Monodelphis domestica. Let C be the smallest clade containing all perissodactyl and all leporid tips. Sub-claim 1 (perissodactyls closer to leporids than to other ungulates) holds iff C contains no artiodactyl tip; sub-claim 2 (leporids closer to perissodactyls than to other rodents) holds iff C contains no rodent tip. Supports if both hold. Independent check: NCBI Taxonomy lineages (efetch) must place Perissodactyla and Leporidae in a shared named clade below Boreoeutheria that excludes Artiodactyla and Rodentia.
fail_criterion: Refutes if C contains both artiodactyl and rodent tips, i.e. perissodactyls nest with other ungulates and leporids nest with rodents rather than with each other (and NCBI Taxonomy places Perissodactyla in Laurasiatheria with Artiodactyla and Leporidae in Glires with Rodentia). Mixed if exactly one sub-claim holds.
interpretation: Thompson's 'more closely related' is read as phylogenetic proximity (more recent common ancestry), the standard modern meaning and the one his transformation argument invokes. 'Other ungulates' is taken in the 1917 sense (Artiodactyla, with Proboscidea and Hyracoidea also included and reported separately); 'other rodents' means Rodentia, since lagomorphs were then classed as rodents (Duplicidentata). The Open Tree synthesis integrates published molecular phylogenies independent of the skull-shape argument; NCBI Taxonomy is a curated classification, not an independent inference, and is used only as a consistency check.
